log.why: Test the leading hypothesis fliC directly to potentially confirm and publish after a single plate.
Treating at 1 µM splits the prior probability mass nearly in half (0.592 vs 0.408), maximizing expected information gain for Ticket 2.
Treating at 3 µM splits the Ticket 2 posterior roughly in half (0.531 vs 0.469), maximizing information while using a free incubator.
Test the leading hypothesis lacZ (0.395 prior) on Ticket 3 so it can incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
Test the leading hypothesis rpoB (0.489) directly on Ticket 3 to utilize an empty incubator before publishing Ticket 1.
Posterior for fliC is 0.871 after E3 showed phenotype lost, high enough to publish immediately.
Posterior for 3 uM is 0.672 after E2 negative and E3 positive; publishing now secures high points and saves plates.
Test top candidate katG directly on urgent Ticket 3.
Testing 10 uM splits the prior probability mass nearly in half (0.437 vs 0.563), maximizing information gain for Ticket 4 while Ticket 3 incubates.
Ticket 3 has high confidence in katG (0.852) and limited time remaining.
E3 at 3 uM splits the posterior mass (~0.515 vs 0.485) and will strongly confirm 10 uM if negative.
E7 tests rpoB and trpE (combined 0.511 prior), splitting the probability mass evenly and pairing with E11 to isolate all top candidates.
Treat at 1 uM to distinguish whether the threshold is 3 uM or <= 1 uM before Ticket 4 expires.
Test the leading hypothesis hisG (0.465) on Ticket 5 directly while waiting for Ticket 4's plate.
Ticket 4 has only 6s left; publishing 1 uM at 0.501 posterior has positive expected value and avoids expiration.
Test the leading candidate recA directly to confirm or rule it out before the ticket and round expire.
With only 10 seconds left on Ticket 5, waiting for E5 risks expiration (-30), whereas publishing recA now has a much higher expected value.
